statement: X06.3's implementation slice (crates/enforcer-memory/src/{adr.rs,architecture.rs,impact.rs,analysis/mod.rs,analysis/query.rs} plus the petgraph Cargo.toml dep and lib.rs module wiring) was salvaged from a dead worktree (agent-ac266c11f9ae4d74f) whose session hit a limit before it could commit. The salvaged content was structurally sound and covered every X06.3 hard requirement (related walk, call-path tracing, reverse dependency traversal, hotspot/degree centrality, architecture overview, ADR store linked to graph nodes, and a D-05-compliant read-only Cypher-subset query DSL with write-verb rejection and a 100k row ceiling) but did not compile and had one real correctness bug once fixed to compile.
why: The dead session had written substantial, well-documented code and inline unit tests but never reached a green build -- salvage-and-fix was far cheaper than a rewrite, and the design (petgraph DiGraph<String,EdgeKind> adjacency view built once per query session over CodeGraph's flat node/edge-list model) matches the workpack's own guidance to prefer petgraph for exactly this class of algorithm.
howToApply: Do not re-derive graph-algorithm code from scratch when a prior worker's WIP exists in a dead worktree -- read it critically first (per the playbook's salvage-triage guidance): this slice needed only (1) a non-generic-to-generic TestResult type alias fix repeated across 3 files' test modules, (2) removing a clippy::only_used_in_recursion #[allow] by refactoring the recursive DFS to a free function taking the graph explicitly (bundling its 6 mutable-state params into a DfsPathState/RelatedWalkState struct to also clear clippy::too_many_arguments without an #[allow]), (3) naming map_err(|_|...) closures to satisfy clippy::map_err_ignore, and (4) replacing .unwrap()/.expect() in adr.rs's own unit tests with ? per this crate's clippy::unwrap_used/expect_used lints (even in test code).

statement: code_graph::CallEdge records only the *file* a call was written in (from_file_id), never the enclosing symbol -- so every Calls edge CodeAdjacency::build produces is shaped file:<path> -> callee-symbol, never symbol -> symbol. The salvaged impact.rs test (diff_impact_finds_transitively_affected_files) asserted file:a.rs was an upstream dependent of file:b.rs purely via CodeAdjacency::reverse_dependents("file:b.rs", ...), but reverse_dependents only follows Direction::Incoming edges into the exact seed id given, and nothing points *into* a bare file id from a call into one of its contained symbols (the file->symbol edge is an outgoing Contains edge, not incoming) -- so the salvaged test failed once the crate actually compiled.
why: This is a real gap in the salvaged analyze_diff_impact, not a fixture/expectation bug: a changed file's blast radius must include callers of every symbol the file *contains*, not just callers of the bare file id, or diff-impact analysis silently under-reports risk for the common case of a file whose functions are called by name from elsewhere.
howToApply: impact::analyze_diff_impact now seeds the reverse walk from the changed file's id AND every symbol node whose file_id matches it (crate::code_graph::CodeGraph::symbol_nodes() filtered by file_id), unions the reverse-dependents of all seeds, and excludes the seed set itself from the reported affected-node list (a file is not 'affected by' its own symbols). Any future caller of CodeAdjacency::reverse_dependents on a file id alone should expect this same gap and multi-seed from the file's own symbols too.

evidence.ref: crates/enforcer-memory/src/impact.rs analyze_diff_impact; failing assertion was 'expected file:a.rs among impacted nodes for changing b.rs, got []' before the fix
